transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-12
Time: 14:00-14:47 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Diego Marquez (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Horizon Head of Data), Liam O'Connor (Horizon DevOps), Sara Patel (Horizon PM), Evan Brody (Horizon Security)

Auto-generated summary: Kickoff for Horizon Labs onboarding. Pilot to start with 2-week soak in staging then pilot to production. Primary concerns: data encryption in transit at rest, KMS integration, network peering, p95 latency under 180ms for single-turn generation.

00:00 Jordan Ellis: okay, uh thanks everyone for joining, I think we can get started, um the plan for today is a rapid immersion, go over the ops runway, security handoff, and agree pilot scope and owners
00:14 Maya Chen: sounds good, we got a couple of folks from infra and security here, mostly to confirm requirements and timelines. quick intro - I'm Maya, Head of Data at Horizon
00:25 Liam O'Connor: Liam, DevOps, I'll be the point for VPC and network peering
00:31 Sara Patel: Sara, Product. We're owning feature integration and rollout plan
00:36 Evan Brody: Evan, Security — interested in KMS key flow and audit logs
00:42 Jordan Ellis: great, on the Redwood side Priya will run through the staging layout and Diego will manage the onboarding timeline and contact points
00:48 Priya Raman: hi everyone — jumping in on the infra layout. for staging we recommend either a dedicated sandbox cluster in our hosted offering or a private VPC deployment; both support KMS and audit logging. the difference is isolation and control over network egress
01:05 Liam O'Connor: when you say private VPC — is that the full private deploy or just private control plane? we have some internal rules that block public outbound on staging so we need to know options.
01:18 Priya Raman: good call. so Private (customer-managed VPC) gives you full control, you manage the peering and routing; Dedicated is a reserved pool but still managed by Redwood with peering; hosted requires less setup but does not meet some of the strict egress policies
01:35 Evan Brody: can you confirm KMS? we need BYOK with a customer key in our HSM. does Redwood support external KMS/HSM or do we have to store keys in Redwood-managed KMS?
01:49 Priya Raman: yes we support external KMS — we have an integration guide. you'll be able to bring a key via standard KMS protocols; there are a few steps for the initial handshake and token exchange. we'll share the KMS integration checklist
02:05 Diego Marquez: (quick note) i'll put the integration doc link in the follow-up, it's in our security pack. also we'll include audit log schema and retention options.
02:12 Sara Patel: timeline — we want pilot in staging by end of October, production by mid-November if all goes well. any blockers you see?
02:24 Jordan Ellis: timeline is tight but doable. main potential blockers: network peering approvals, KMS sign-off, and sample workload confirmation — we need your prompt set and expected throughput pattern
02:38 Maya Chen: for throughput — initial pilot is mostly user-facing chat with 10 qps peak, mostly short-turns, sequence lengths under 512 tokens. p95 latency target is 180ms end-to-end (including network), cost target TBD
02:57 Priya Raman: that use-case fits continuous batching well; we'll recommend batching and a small KV cache footprint. also quantization suggestions if cost becomes an issue.
03:13 Liam O'Connor: how invasive is the network setup? I'm concerned about firewall rules — we have to route through our NATs and firewall to inspect egress
03:24 Priya Raman: for VPC peering we typically need a single peering connection and a couple ip ranges. firewall-wise, allow outbound to Redwood control plane CIDRs and TLS certs; if you're using private, you'll manage routing. we can provide a proposed ip checklist
03:44 Evan Brody: audit logs — what granularity? we need token-level logging turned off but event-level, who-called-what, and model metadata for compliance
03:58 Diego Marquez: we can set token-level redaction by default. audit logs include request metadata, model version, latency, user id (if passed) — retention configurable per account tier
04:16 Sara Patel: are there existing connectors for our stack? we're running feature flags with LaunchDarkly, infra on AWS with EKS, and metaflow for pipelines
04:29 Priya Raman: yes — we have SDKs for Node/Python and a webhook connector for LaunchDarkly for event-based rollouts. EKS is a supported infra for private deploys and we have helm charts for easier install
04:45 Maya Chen: about quality monitoring — can Redwood run evals against a static prompt set and alert if regressions occur? we need guardrails before we flip to prod
04:58 Diego Marquez: absolutely — Redwood Optimize can run prompt-set based quality checks and tie regression alerts to a Slack channel or PagerDuty. we'll propose thresholds and a cadence during the pilot
05:14 Jordan Ellis: quick note on deployment modes tradeoffs: Hosted = fastest to start, less isolation; Dedicated = reserved compute, predictable throughput and lower noisy-neighbor risk; Private = customer-managed, highest control for security teams.
05:34 Liam O'Connor: cost? if we commit to Dedicated for pilot then scale, what are commit terms?
05:41 Jordan Ellis: we'll follow up with pricing spreadsheet comparing per-token hosted vs monthly committed for Dedicated; pilot discounts often available for early usage, we'll include an example for 6-month commit
05:55 Sara Patel: for pilot success criteria let's set a few measurable items: p95 latency under 180ms in staging, no PII leakage detected in 2-week soak, and integration with SSO + RBAC for internal users
06:12 Maya Chen: agreed. also need a rollback plan if models regress — can we pin model versions and roll back automatically?
06:20 Priya Raman: yes — rollouts support canary and automatic fallback to previous model variant. we'll show the rollout UI in the next demo
06:32 Evan Brody: SSO — we use SAML with Okta. what's Redwood's support level?
06:38 Diego Marquez: SAML SSO with Okta is supported; we'll need metadata exchange and role mappings for RBAC. Diego will coordinate with your identity engineer
06:49 Jordan Ellis: (interrupting) quick question — any concerns about data residency? Horizon has eu-data residency needs for EU customers
06:55 Maya Chen: yes we need EU residency for EU traffic; pilot will be in us-east for internal testing but production must be region-aware
07:08 Priya Raman: we can route EU traffic to our eu region. configurations are per-route; we'll capture that in the routing policy doc
07:22 Liam O'Connor: latency numbers — are the p95 figures measured at Redwood edge or end-to-end? we need end-to-end for SLA
07:30 Priya Raman: good point. our console reports both server-side token latency and end-to-end; for your SLA we'll instrument a synthetic probe from your VPC to measure end-to-end
07:42 Sara Patel: any gotchas with KV cache and short-turn chat? we saw some models cache prefix unexpectedly in another vendor
07:52 Priya Raman: Redwood's KV cache is per-conversation and key rotation is managed. there are some heuristics — we'll include cache behavior notes in the engineering doc. sometimes transcription pulls back as K V cash in auto docs — sorry, it's K V cache
08:06 (laughter)
08:10 Diego Marquez: logistics — Diego will be your onboarding lead, weekly check-ins Wed 30 mins. first soak test w/c Oct 25, rollout target Nov 15.
08:25 Jordan Ellis: i will send contract and security pack by Friday; Priya will share staging network checklist and helm charts
08:33 Evan Brody: can you also include any pen-test reports or SOC2 scope? we need those for procurement
08:40 Jordan Ellis: yes, SOC2 Type II report excerpt and pen-test summary will be in the security pack.
08:47 Priya Raman: anything else from the team?
08:50 Maya Chen: just to confirm — we'll provide prompt set and throughput pattern by Monday
08:55 Liam O'Connor: i'll open a ticket with our infra team to review peering — expect answers by Oct 17
09:03 Sara Patel: great, looking forward to the demo of the rollout UI and the performance report
09:10 Jordan Ellis: perfect. recap then: deliverables — security pack + contract (Jordan), staging network checklist + helm charts (Priya), test deployment + soak plan (Priya/Diego), Horizon to provide prompts + latency targets (Maya/Liam). we'll set weekly Wed checkpoints.
09:34 Diego Marquez: i'll book the weekly sync and put calendar invites.
09:40 Jordan Ellis: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the notes with links.

References shared in meeting: Security pack link (sent after): https://redwood.example.com/sec-pack/horizon-2027, Staging network checklist (to be attached), Pilot pricing spreadsheet (will be attached)

End of transcript.
